hints: Because the data is discrete (number of incorrect notes), class intervals have continuous boundaries at $\pm 0.5$: $0.5$ to $5.5$, $5.5$ to $10.5$, $10.5$ to $20.5$, $20.5$ to $40.5$, and $40.5$ to $70.5$.

Calculate frequency density for each class using $\text{Frequency density} = \dfrac{\text{Frequency}}{\text{Class width}}$: $\frac{10}{5} = 2.0$, $\frac{5}{5} = 1.0$, $\frac{26}{10} = 2.6$, $\frac{32}{20} = 1.6$, $\frac{18}{30} = 0.6$.
Plot a histogram with frequency density on the vertical axis and number of incorrect notes on the horizontal axis.
walkthrough:
Find the class boundaries, class widths, and frequency densities for each interval:
$$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|c|}\hline \text{Class} & \text{Boundaries} & \text{Width } w & \text{Frequency } f & \text{Frequency density } (f/w) \\\hline 1\text{--}5 & 0.5\text{--}5.5 & 5 & 10 & 2.0 \\ 6\text{--}10 & 5.5\text{--}10.5 & 5 & 5 & 1.0 \\ 11\text{--}20 & 10.5\text{--}20.5 & 10 & 26 & 2.6 \\ 21\text{--}40 & 20.5\text{--}40.5 & 20 & 32 & 1.6 \\ 41\text{--}70 & 40.5\text{--}70.5 & 30 & 18 & 0.6 \\\hline\end{array}$$
Draw the histogram with a linear vertical scale for frequency density starting at 0, bars meeting at continuous boundaries $0.5, 5.5, 10.5, 20.5, 40.5, 70.5$, and clearly labelled axes.
teacher_walkthrough: We are asked to draw a histogram representing the number of incorrect notes played by 91 pianists.

Step 1: Determine class boundaries and class widths.
Since the number of incorrect notes is a discrete count, we use continuity boundaries halfway between consecutive integer classes:
- $1-5$: boundaries $[0.5, 5.5]$, width $= 5.5 - 0.5 = 5$
- $6-10$: boundaries $[5.5, 10.5]$, width $= 10.5 - 5.5 = 5$
- $11-20$: boundaries $[10.5, 20.5]$, width $= 20.5 - 10.5 = 10$
- $21-40$: boundaries $[20.5, 40.5]$, width $= 40.5 - 20.5 = 20$
- $41-70$: boundaries $[40.5, 70.5]$, width $= 70.5 - 40.5 = 30$

Step 2: Calculate the frequency density for each bar using $\text{Frequency density} = \frac{\text{Frequency}}{\text{Class width}}$:
- Class $1-5$: $\frac{10}{5} = 2.0$
- Class $6-10$: $\frac{5}{5} = 1.0$
- Class $11-20$: $\frac{26}{10} = 2.6$
- Class $21-40$: $\frac{32}{20} = 1.6$
- Class $41-70$: $\frac{18}{30} = 0.6$

Step 3: Plot the histogram.
- Horizontal axis: Number of incorrect notes, with values from 0 to 75.
- Vertical axis: Frequency density, linear scale from 0 to 3.0.
- Draw 5 contiguous rectangles with heights $2.0, 1.0, 2.6, 1.6, 0.6$ over their respective boundary intervals.

hints: With total frequency $n = 91$, find the cumulative frequencies: 10, 15, 41, 73, 91.
The lower quartile position is $\frac{91}{4} = 22.75$, which falls in cumulative frequency interval $16$ to $41$, corresponding to class $11-20$.
The upper quartile position is $\frac{3 \times 91}{4} = 68.25$, which falls in cumulative frequency interval $42$ to $73$, corresponding to class $21-40$.

To find the greatest possible interquartile range, take the maximum possible value in the upper quartile interval ($40$) minus the minimum possible value in the lower quartile interval ($11$): $40 - 11 = 29$.
walkthrough:
Calculate the cumulative frequencies for the 91 pianists:
$$\begin{array}{c|ccccc}\text{Class} & 1\text{--}5 & 6\text{--}10 & 11\text{--}20 & 21\text{--}40 & 41\text{--}70 \\\hline \text{Frequency} & 10 & 5 & 26 & 32 & 18 \\ \text{Cumulative Frequency} & 10 & 15 & 41 & 73 & 91 \end{array}$$

Identify the quartile positions:
$$\text{Position of } Q_1 = 0.25 \times 91 = 22.75 \implies Q_1 \text{ lies in class } 11\text{--}20$$
$$\text{Position of } Q_3 = 0.75 \times 91 = 68.25 \implies Q_3 \text{ lies in class } 21\text{--}40$$

Calculate the greatest possible value of the interquartile range:
$$\text{Greatest IQR} = \max(Q_3) - \min(Q_1) = 40 - 11 = 29$$
teacher_walkthrough: We need to identify the class intervals containing the lower quartile ($Q_1$) and upper quartile ($Q_3$), and then find the greatest possible value of the IQR.

Step 1: Set up cumulative frequencies for the $n = 91$ pianists:
- Class $1-5$: frequency $10 \implies$ cumulative frequency $10$
- Class $6-10$: frequency $5 \implies$ cumulative frequency $15$
- Class $11-20$: frequency $26 \implies$ cumulative frequency $41$
- Class $21-40$: frequency $32 \implies$ cumulative frequency $73$
- Class $41-70$: frequency $18 \implies$ cumulative frequency $91$

Step 2: Locate the lower quartile interval ($Q_1$):
$$\text{Rank of } Q_1 = \frac{91}{4} = 22.75$$
Since $15 < 22.75 \le 41$, $Q_1$ lies in the interval $11-20$.

Step 3: Locate the upper quartile interval ($Q_3$):
$$\text{Rank of } Q_3 = \frac{3 \times 91}{4} = 68.25$$
Since $41 < 68.25 \le 73$, $Q_3$ lies in the interval $21-40$.

Step 4: Find the greatest possible interquartile range:
$$\text{IQR} = Q_3 - Q_1$$
To make this difference as large as possible, we take the largest possible value for $Q_3$ and the smallest possible value for $Q_1$:
- The largest integer in the class $21-40$ is $40$.
- The smallest integer in the class $11-20$ is $11$.
$$\text{Greatest possible IQR} = 40 - 11 = 29$$

hints: Multiply each midpoint by its frequency to find $\sum fx$: $3(10) + 8(5) + 15.5(26) + 30.5(32) + 55.5(18)$.
Divide by total frequency $\sum f = 91$: $\frac{2448}{91} \approx 26.9$ incorrect notes.
walkthrough:
Determine the midpoints ($x$) of the class intervals:
$$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|}\hline \text{Interval} & \text{Midpoint } x & \text{Frequency } f & f x \\\hline 1\text{--}5 & 3 & 10 & 30 \\ 6\text{--}10 & 8 & 5 & 40 \\ 11\text{--}20 & 15.5 & 26 & 403 \\ 21\text{--}40 & 30.5 & 32 & 976 \\ 41\text{--}70 & 55.5 & 18 & 999 \\\hline \text{Total} & & 91 & 2448 \\\hline\end{array}$$

Compute the estimated mean using $\bar{x} = \dfrac{\sum fx}{\sum f}$:
$$\bar{x} = \dfrac{2448}{91} \approx 26.9011 \approx 26.9\text{ incorrect notes}$$
teacher_walkthrough: We need to calculate an estimate for the mean number of incorrect notes.

Step 2: Multiply each midpoint by its frequency ($f \times x$):
- $10 \times 3 = 30$
- $5 \times 8 = 40$
- $26 \times 15.5 = 403$
- $32 \times 30.5 = 976$
- $18 \times 55.5 = 999$

Step 4: Divide by the total frequency $\sum f = 91$:
$$\bar{x} = \frac{\sum fx}{\sum f} = \frac{2448}{91} \approx 26.90109...$$
Rounding to 3 significant figures gives $26.9$ incorrect notes.
